trans-unit.source: The Hour of Matins
trans-unit.note: Title of Chapter I. Canonical-hour names follow the termbase.

trans-unit.source: Page-boy Emmerich
Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The Free City of Kessendorf. Winter, in the ninth year of the Long Muster.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 1 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The river has frozen twice. The pyres outside the east gate have not gone out since autumn.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 2 of 10.

trans-unit.source: So. You are the new sawbones the Guild sent me. Kreuzer, is it?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 3 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Apothecary-surgeon, sworn at Weissburg. I have my letters, Master Haller—
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 4 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Letters. Letters don’t stop a man bleeding into the straw. Hands do. Show me your hands.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 5 of 10.

trans-unit.source: …Steady enough. Sister! Our young doctor has arrived just in time for the Tuesday knife-fights.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 6 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Sister Ilse, of the Merciful Order. I keep the instruments, the ledgers, and the Master’s temper.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 7 of 10.

trans-unit.source: There’s a drover on the table already. Somebody at the Gilded Goose disagreed with his dice.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 8 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Knife wounds. Simple work. Stitch him, drain him, salve him. I’ll watch.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 9 of 10.

trans-unit.source: And Kreuzer — in this hospice we do not lose patients to simple work.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 10 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the next morning
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The drover lived. He paid in turnips and a promise not to gamble again. He will break it by Friday.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 1 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Make way! Make way, damn you! Surgeon! Where’s the surgeon?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 2 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Captain Mauer of the Watch. Lower your voice, Captain, this is a house of mercy.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 3 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Horned raiders hit the timber-road caravan at dawn. We drove them off, but young Pieter took a shaft in the side.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 4 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Beast-folk fletch their arrows with barbed heads. Rip one straight out and you’ll tear half his side with it.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 5 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Nick the flesh at the entry with the lancet — twice — to free the barbs. Then pull. Cleanly.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 6 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — noon
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Pieter will keep his side, and his opinion of beast-folk.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 1 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, the gunsmiths’ quarter. An apprentice was proving a new handgun barrel and it burst in his hands.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 2 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Burns across the chest and lead fragments driven under the skin.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 3 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Powder burns. The charred skin is dead — pluck the eschar away with tongs before you salve, or it festers.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 4 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The shot is in deep. You’ll have to open him. Trace the line I’ve inked, and keep your hand true.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 5 of 6.

trans-unit.source: He’s lost blood already. If his pulse flags, the tincture — hold it to the flesh and let it take.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 6 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — dusk
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Word travels fast in Kessendorf. By dusk, there is a queue at the hospice door.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 1 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Doctor… this one was found in the Tanners’ Rows. Swellings at the neck and groin. Fever. Maggots in a sore.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 2 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Buboes. Lance them before they burst, draw off the pus, and salve the wound. Rot-patches creep back if you dawdle.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 3 of 7.

trans-unit.source: And the grubs — the cautery brand. Hold it on them until they stop wriggling. Mind you don’t sear good flesh.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 4 of 7.

trans-unit.source: A plague case. In the city. How very interesting.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 5 of 7.

trans-unit.source: …Inquisitor Stroh. Of the Ash Tribunal.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 6 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Please, do carry on, Doctor. I only wish to watch. Pestilence so often has a sponsor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 7 of 7.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the small hours
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Near midnight a carriage without a crest stops at the gate. A page-boy is carried in, raving.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 1 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The choir… they’re singing in me… make them stop singing…
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 2 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, look at his chest. Those marks — they’re moving.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 3 of 8.

trans-unit.source: …That is no disease. Those are sigils. Someone has written on this boy.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 4 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Kreuzer. Listen to me carefully. Sear the sigils out with the brand — trace every stroke.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 5 of 8.

trans-unit.source: And if something… answers… when you do — there is an old apothecary’s rite. The Litany of Stillness.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 6 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Trace the five-pointed star and still your heart. For a few breaths, the world will wait for you.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 7 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Do not do it where the Inquisitor can see. The Tribunal does not distinguish between a prayer and a spell.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 8 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — before dawn
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The thing in the boy’s chest came apart like wet ash. The boy sleeps. He no longer hears singing.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 1 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Doctor… after it broke, a word was left seared into the flesh. Matins.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 2 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The first of the canonical hours. The first prayer of the night.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 3 of 10.

trans-unit.source: A curse that lives and fights like a beast, and signs itself like a psalm. A Malison.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 4 of 10.

trans-unit.source: And if this was Matins… then somewhere, someone is already writing Lauds.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 5 of 10.

trans-unit.source: A remarkable recovery, Doctor. Remarkable.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 6 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Tell me — at the end, your hands moved so very quickly. Almost as if time itself were… obliging you.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 7 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Practice, Inquisitor. And the grace of Saint Ildra.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 8 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Of course. The grace of the Saint. I shall pray on it.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 9 of 10.

trans-unit.source: END OF CHAPTER I — THE HOUR OF MATINS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 10 of 10.

trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Jost, drover
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Knife wounds to the forearm and flank after a dice dispute. Moderate bleeding.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The Barbed Shaft
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Pieter, militiaman
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Barbed arrow lodged in the left flank; crossbow bolt in the thigh. Raider ambush.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: Powder Burns
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Anno, gunsmith’s apprentice
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Burst-barrel injury: powder burns across the chest, lead fragments embedded beneath the skin.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: Pestilent Humours
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Unknown vagrant, Tanners’ Rows
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Plague buboes, spreading rot and an infested sore. High fever.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The Hour of Matins
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Emmerich, page-boy
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Unknown. Moving marks on the chest. Delirium. “The choir is singing in me.”
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: Two deep cuts. Take the gut thread and zig-zag across each wound to stitch it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Cross the wound again and again, moving along it. One smooth stroke earns the best marks.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Blood’s pooling. Hold the leech-pipe over it to draw it off.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: You can’t stitch through a pool of blood — drain first.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Just nicks left. Brush Saint’s Salve over the small ones — no need for thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: The arrow’s barbed. Lancet first — two nicks at the entry wound. Then seize it with the tongs and pull it well clear.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: Then drain and stitch the wound it leaves.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: The bolt in his thigh has no barbs. Tongs, and pull it straight out.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: Quick, clean pulls earn the best marks.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: His pulse is weak already. Hold the tincture to the flesh to steady him if you need it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Burns first. Pluck the black eschar away with the tongs, then salve the raw flesh.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now open him along the inked line with the lancet. Keep to the line — start at the glowing end.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: There — the shot. Pull each ball out with the tongs.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Lance each bubo with a single touch of the lancet before it bursts. Then drain the pus and salve it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Grubs in the sore! The cautery brand — hold it on each one until it stops moving.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Don’t linger on bare flesh with the brand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: The rot’s spreading. Salve every patch — quickly, it creeps back.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Those sigils are draining him. Trace every stroke of each one with the brand to sear it out.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Something is moving beneath the skin. We have to open him. The lancet — along the line.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Saints preserve us… what is that?
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Doctor — if ever there were a time for the Litany, it is now. Draw the star with the right hand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: It’s gone. Tend the wounds it left.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 5 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: The Hour of Lauds
trans-unit.note: Title of Chapter II. Canonical-hour names follow the termbase.

trans-unit.source: Orsa Flintvein
Orsa Flintvein
Orsa Flintvein
The cantor
The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 1 of 8.

trans-unit.source: A week after the page-boy, a writ arrives with the Watch’s seal: the hospice’s surgeon is requisitioned for the muster.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 2 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Don’t look at me like that, Doctor. I didn’t ask for you. The Inquisitor “suggested” it to the Burgomaster.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 3 of 8.

trans-unit.source: So he can watch you somewhere with fewer witnesses.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 4 of 8.

trans-unit.source: We’re clearing the Grauwald of raiders before the spring caravans. My lads need a surgeon more than a city needs rumours.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 5 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Speaking of which — the scouts came back. Two of them. Something followed them out of the barrow-fields.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 6 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, it’s a gravehound bite. Claw rakes across the back, and — look — it left its teeth in him.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 7 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Corpse-eaters carry a venom in their spit. Hold the tincture to the bite itself and it will draw the poison.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 8 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — afternoon
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The scout will limp, but he will limp home.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 1 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Put me down, you long-legged oafs! I can walk! I can… mostly walk.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 2 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Dwarf prospector. Her crew was working a seam in the hills when it caved in.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 3 of 7.

trans-unit.source: The rock went black, Doctor. Black and wrong, like a bruise in the stone. It sang when we struck it. Then it burst.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 4 of 7.

trans-unit.source: There are shards under her skin that I can’t see — but the flesh around them is spoiling.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 5 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Master Haller sent this with me. His old Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh and it shows what hides beneath.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 6 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Dwarf hide’s thicker than yours, lad. You’ll want a strong arm on that thread.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 7 of 7.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — night
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Orsa sleeps in the supply wagon, snoring like a bellows. She has promised to name a mine after the Doctor. It will probably be a bad one.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Forager. Went to check his snares near the old web-trees. We found him wrapped up like a Martinmas ham.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: A web-spinner bite. Venom, spreading fast. And these lumps under the skin… Saints. She laid in him.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 3 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Lance the sacs before they hatch, Doctor, and sear what spills out. If they hatch on their own, they’ll scatter.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 4 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — before midnight
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Doctor. I have brought you a gift.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 1 of 7.

trans-unit.source: Two of the Inquisitor’s men drag a thin, grey-robed figure into the light. His chest is a lattice of glowing sigils.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 2 of 7.

trans-unit.source: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir. We took him in the barrow-fields, singing to the dead.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 3 of 7.

trans-unit.source: The moment he began to confess, those marks ignited. His masters would rather he burned than spoke.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 4 of 7.

trans-unit.source: He also swallowed something. You will keep him alive. I have questions, and the dead are poor at answering them.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 5 of 7.

trans-unit.source: …Doctor. Whatever he is, he’s a patient.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 6 of 7.

trans-unit.source: On the table. Now.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 7 of 7.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — dawn
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The cantor lived long enough to whisper one thing, before Stroh’s men took him away.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 1 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Lauds… is sung at dawn… with the muster… under the banner…
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 2 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The dawn muster? That’s now — the whole company’s singing the morning hymn—
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 3 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Across the camp, the hymn falters. The standard-bearer drops to his knees, the banner falling across him.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 4 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Doctor! It’s Jorg, the standard-bearer — his chest is moving… it’s singing back!
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 5 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Clear a table. Sister — every instrument we have.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 6 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — morning
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The singing stops. The standard-bearer breathes. In the flesh over his heart, a single word: LAUDS.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 1 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Two of them now. Matins in the city, Lauds in my own camp. Someone is keeping time, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 2 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Six more hours to the full Office. Prime. Terce. Sext. None. Vespers. Compline.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 3 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Doctor Kreuzer.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 4 of 9.

trans-unit.source: When that thing screamed, every candle in this tent stopped flickering. The flames stood still. For eight heartbeats.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 5 of 9.

trans-unit.source: I counted.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 6 of 9.

trans-unit.source: …The morning air is very still, Inquisitor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 7 of 9.

trans-unit.source: So it is. We will speak at length, you and I. After Prime.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 8 of 9.

trans-unit.source: END OF CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 9 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Gravehound
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Tomas, scout
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Mauled by a corpse-eating hound. Claw rakes across the back, fangs lodged in the shoulder, venom spreading from the bite.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The Black Seam
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Orsa Flintvein, dwarf prospector
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Cave-in at a hexstone seam. Shards driven beneath the skin, invisible to the eye. Surrounding flesh spoiling.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: Brood-Mother’s Kiss
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Henning, forager
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Web-spinner bite. Neurotoxic venom spreading from the neck; several egg sacs laid beneath the skin.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The Silenced Cantor
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Silence-sigils igniting across the chest (hexfire). Self-administered poison. Prisoner of the Ash Tribunal.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The Hour of Lauds
trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Jorg, standard-bearer
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Collapsed during the dawn hymn. Something beneath the sternum is singing.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The venom first — hold the tincture on the bite until it takes.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: The longer it spreads, the harder it drags on him.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now the fangs. Tongs — pull each one clear.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Claw rakes. Three deep lines — drain and stitch each.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Rock splinters on the surface first. Tongs.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now — the Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh; where something hides, it shimmers.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Hold it still over the shimmer to bring the shard to light, then pull it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Clean up the spoiled flesh and any wounds left.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Venom from two bites. Tincture on each, quickly.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: The sacs — lance each one with a single touch, then sear the hatchlings with the brand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: Mind the ones that are close to hatching.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: One more sac, deeper. Use the lens to find it, then open it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: And he’s taken a fever-bubo from the bite — lance and cleanse it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: The poison he swallowed — tincture, now, or he’s gone before we start.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: Those sigils are burning him from within. Sear each one out — every stroke.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: The hexfire burns. Pluck the eschar, then salve them.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: Maggots in an old sore — the Tribunal’s cells are filthy. Brand them.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: We have to open him — along the line, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Saints… it has a choir. Those little lights are its Voices — hold the brand on each as it circles.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Silence all of them and its heart will be bare.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: It’s done. Tend what it left of him.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Close him up. Gently — he has a banner to carry.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Too much blood — draw it off with the leech-pipe before you stitch!
The hexstone is corrupting the flesh around it — get it out!
Barbed! Nick the flesh at the entry with the lancet before you pull.
The dead flesh is off. Now salve the raw burn.
Pluck away the charred eschar with the tongs first!
Draw off the pus before you salve it.
The choir is silenced — its heart is bare! Brand it, now!
It’s calling its Voices back!
It’s singing — every verse tears him open! Stitch the cuts as they come!
There! It’s surfacing — finish it!
The Voices shield it. Silence them first — hold the brand on each as it circles.
It’s gone under the skin! The Scrying Lens — hunt it down!
It shattered — hexstone, everywhere! Get every shard out before it spoils him!
Spiderlings! Brand them before they scatter!
Its shroud has parted — sear it with the brand, now!
It’s tearing the flesh as it moves! Stitch those wounds!
The brand can’t touch it while it’s veiled. Wait for the shroud to part!
It’s shedding hexlings! Burn them before they feed!
It’s splitting apart! Seize every shard with the tongs and cast it out — before they rejoin!
Careful! The brand is searing healthy flesh!
Vitals are failing! Use the tincture, Doctor!
The operation is complete.
Instruments ready, Doctor.
